fact: Certain fungi can hijack the nervous systems of ants, turning the ants into ‘zombies’ that are forced to climb to the precise height of a plant with the right conditions for the fungus to grow.

retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: Certain fungi have the remarkable ability to control the behavior of insects, such as ants and flies, by manipulating their nervous systems. One fungus, Entomophthora muscae, causes infected fruit flies to climb to elevated spots and latch onto plants, creating an ideal environment for the fungus to grow. Researchers studied this interaction by infecting fruit flies with a lab strain of the fungus and monitoring changes in gene activity. They found that the flies mounted a strong immune defense shortly after infection, while the fungus began invading the nervous system early on, reshaping itself into a deadly form. Within a few days, the fungus spread throughout the flies’ bodies, ultimately leading to their death.

retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: In dry caves of southeastern Brazil, a group of insects named Neotrogla have egg-producing females with penises and sperm-producing males with vaginas. The sex roles of the Brazilian cave insects Neotrogla are reversed, with females competing over males and males being selective of their female partners. The sex role reversal in Neotrogla likely evolved because the males’ semen represents a rich and reliable source of energy within a nutrient-poor cave environment. The brains of toddlers with little interest in social stimuli receive less social input than the brains of other toddlers. Among children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), there are large differences in children's interest in the social world. The majority of toddlers, including most toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), spent more time looking at the children than the shapes. About 20% of toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) spent most of their time looking at the shapes instead of the children. Toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who spent most of their time looking at shapes had the most severe social symptoms. measured the brain activity of toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) while the toddlers slept. During sleep or rest, the brain shows stereotyped patterns of activity. Groups of brain regions that work together, such as those involved in vision, fire in synchrony during sleep or rest. Toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who preferred looking at shapes over people showed different patterns of brain activity while asleep compared to other children. In toddlers with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) who preferred shapes, brain networks involved in social skills were less likely to coordinate their activity with networks that support vision and attention. At present, all children who receive a diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) receive much the same behavioral therapy.

The spliceosome is a complex molecular machine formed of numerous parts, excluding one known as U1 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (U1 snRNP), that must come together. retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: As cells in our body grow and divide, their RNA can experience changes or damage. Most of the mutations in DNA are harmless or quickly fixed by the human body. Sometimes a mutation can trigger a chain of genetic events that drives the cells to multiply uncontrollably, which leads to tumors. Identifying driver mutations is complex but key to understanding how cancers start and can be fought. Breast cancer is the second most common type of cancer diagnosed in women worldwide. If too many chaperone proteins are present in the cell, they may slow down the protein folding process. If a cell experiences stressful conditions or if there is a sudden demand for more proteins to be made, protein folding can be disrupted. retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: Malaria parasites enter the host via the bloodstream, where they are deposited by infected mosquitoes as the mosquitoes look for blood. Malaria parasites must exit the liver to reach the skin, where the parasites multiply and ultimately infect red blood cells, causing the symptoms of malaria. In the skin, malaria parasites must move to find blood vessels that they enter to travel via the blood circulation to the liver. Only about 10–20% of malaria parasites make it out of the skin, making the skin a bottleneck for the parasite. Scientists have been working to develop vaccines that would protect people against malaria. One way these could work would be to stop malaria parasites from leaving the blood vessels and entering

Malaria parasites slow down when they come close to a blood vessel and move on or around the vessel for some time before entering it. Hopp et al. investigated how two malaria parasite mutants move through mouse skin. Cells contain biological machines that refold or break down misfolded proteins. The activity of ATP-dependent AAA+ proteases needs to be tightly controlled because breaking down the wrong proteins can harm cells. ATP-dependent AAA+ proteases form ring-shaped assemblies that are composed of AAA+ proteins and an associated peptidase. In bacteria, the AAA+ protein called ClpC can be crucial for resisting stress and infecting host cells. ClpC have a “coiled coil” structure, and they interact via their ends in a head-to-head manner. In the activated state, ClpC cannot interact with its partner peptidase and the shape of the assembly shields the sites where adapter proteins can bind. The shielding of adapter protein binding sites in the repressed state renders ClpC inactive. ClpC proteins with mutations to the middle domain that prevent the repressed state from forming remain in a constantly active state that is highly toxic to bacteria. Bacteria are increasingly evolving to enhance the effects of the antibiotics commonly used to treat infections. Millions of tons of fertiliser are applied to agricultural land each year to maintain crop yields because essential elements such as nitrogen and phosphate are often in short supply. Another way for plants to lose access to scarce nutrients is to form symbiotic relationships with microorganisms that live in the soil. Legumes such as peas, beans, and clovers can form relationships with bacteria that convert nitrogen from the air into ammonia, which the plants then use to make molecules such as DNA and proteins. retrieved_chunks.chunk_text: The immune system helps animals fight off bacterial infections, but responding to these threats uses surprisingly little energy and can sometimes cause harm if overactivated. Because of this, avoiding contact with harmful bacteria in the first place might be a safer way to stay healthy. Research has found that fruit flies, similar to humans, use their sense of smell to detect dangers in their surroundings, but it was unclear if they could taste harmful bacteria. New experiments reveal that fruit flies can actually sense bacterial molecules called lipopolysaccharides (LPS) through taste, triggering bitter-sensitive nerves that lead them to avoid contaminated food and egg-laying sites. This detection relies on a protein called TRPA1, which differs from the one humans use to
